Okay so to answer your question: First of all, thins thing called "affirmative action" means different things in the context of college admissions and hiring. In college admissions, you're allowed to examine race and gender as part of a larger set of things you're looking at, which means that sometimes a less qualified applicant gets admitted because of race or gender. In employment contexts, you're never allowed to admit a less qualified applicant on the basis of race or gender. Even if it's in a 'positive' direction (whatever that means). So hopefully that answers your question about what is/isn't allowed for discrimination both for and against gays in employment.

But wait, what's this 'affirmative action' thing that some employers (such as federal contractors) are doing? Well, actually it's basically looking at the hiring system and seeing where some kinds of candidates have roadblocks, and eliminating them. For example, maybe you experiment and give your HR department identical resumes for male and female applicants, and it turns out that they throw out the female resumes more often. In this case, you can figure out why this is happening (maybe your HR staff is biased) and fix it (maybe you force them to take a class). What if you notice your interviewers approve female applicants more often than male applicants for that nursing position? Same thing: Maybe your interviewers are being more harsh on male applicants than they should, since they don't see male applicants as potential nurses, but you could fix this by asking them to rate interviewees on objective aspects which are less likely to be influenced by gender.

And yes, I get that here the context is discrimination based on sexual orientation, not gender/race. But it's kind of easier to explain the principles of affirmative action using gender (since sexual orientation will more often than not come up after hiring decisions are made). To be honest this ruling probably won't affect hiring much; what it will probably affect is firing people because it suddenly comes out that they are gay, or passing them over for promotions, which unlike pro-gay discrimination is an actual, documented issue that is happening today.
